diameterInterpretation: Approximate scale from a thermal diameter of 24.38 ± 0.48 km. Quoted uncertainty does not fully include thermal-model and viewing-geometry effects.

calibration.uncertaintyMeaning: Published thermal-model uncertainty propagated from flux, absolute magnitude and slope parameter. Shape, spin/aspect and fixed thermophysical assumptions are not fully included.
calibration.systematicMeaning: Usui 2011 notes additional unquantified model effects and typically a few to approximately 10% rotation-related size uncertainty; this is not an object-specific interval.
calibration.quantity: Standard Thermal Model mean effective spherical diameter
calibration.reference: Usui et al. (2011), PASJ63,1117-1138, AcuA V1
calibration.selectionReason: Direct AKARI measured thermal diameter is available; no diameter exists in current SBDB or the queried NEOWISE V2 rows. No assumed-albedo size is used.
calibration.formula: scaleKmPerSourceUnit = diameterKm / cbrt(6 * signedSourceVolume / pi); meterScale =1000*scaleKmPerSourceUnit. Original shape coordinates are preserved.
limitations: The thermal effective spherical diameter is used as an approximate volume-equivalent display scale; no joint shape/thermal inversion or independently measured volume is implied.
AKARI catalog ±0.48 km omits unquantified spin/aspect and thermal-model effects; Reinmuthia is elongated, so absolute scale remains approximate.
calibration.sourceLabel: Usui et al. (2011), PASJ63,1117-1138, AcuA V1
calibration.visibleDescription: Approximate scale from a thermal diameter of 24.38 ± 0.48 km. Quoted uncertainty does not fully include thermal-model and viewing-geometry effects.

modelLimitations: The convex inversion resolves the broad shape; craters and concavities are unresolved. The selected pole is one of the published alternatives.
